quests.ruleExplanation: 'Where' is a relative adverb that stands in for 'in which' (or 'at which'), pointing back to a place - here, 'the cafe.'

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Where vs Which/That for Places
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence here is grammatically correct?
quests.targetClause: The restaurant that I recommended to my friends closed down.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence here is grammatically correct?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Recommended' needs a direct object (something being recommended), not a location - so 'where' is wrong here even though the restaurant is a place. 'That' correctly marks the restaurant as the object of 'recommended.'
quests.nativeTip: Check what 'recommended' needs - a location to happen in, or a direct object to receive the action?

quests.completedSentence: Which version below is grammatically correct?

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: When vs Which/That for Time
quests.questionSentence: 2019 was the year ___ I'll never forget.
quests.completedSentence: 2019 was the year that I'll never forget.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Forget' needs a direct object (something being forgotten), not a time period, so 'when' doesn't fit here even though the antecedent is a year. 'That' correctly marks the year as the object of 'forget.'
quests.nativeTip: Check what 'forget' needs - a time period to happen during, or a direct object to receive the action?

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Adverb of Time (when)

quests.completedSentence: 2019 was the year when I finally graduated.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'When' correctly refers to '2019,' a time, and doesn't require a direct object the way 'forget' did in the previous example; 'graduated' is a complete action on its own.
quests.nativeTip: 'Graduated' doesn't need a direct object here - check which word naturally points back to a time without needing an extra preposition.

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Adverbs Cannot Be Subjects
quests.questionSentence: The day ___ upended our entire plan came out of nowhere.
quests.completedSentence: The day that upended our entire plan came out of nowhere.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Upended' has no other subject, so the blank must supply one - but relative adverbs like 'when' can never act as a clause's subject. Only 'that' (or 'which') can, so 'that' is correct here despite the day being a time.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether 'upended' already has a subject elsewhere - if the blank itself must be the subject, could an adverb like 'when' possibly do that job?
